test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Mechanic Diesel) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A line in an engineering drawing is the ____________.

options.text: one-dimensional figure, which has length but no width
dimensionless location in space or on a drawing sheet that has no width, height, or depth
three-dimensional object with length, breadth, and height
closed curve where all points are the same distance from a fixed centre point

solution:
__**Explanation:**__

A line in an engineering drawing is a fundamental graphical element used to represent the shape, size, and configuration of an object. Lines are essential components of technical drawings, and they help communicate the geometry and details of the design to engineers, manufacturers, and other stakeholders.

In technical terms, a line is a one-dimensional figure characterized by having length but no width. It is one of the simplest geometric entities and serves as the basis for constructing more complex shapes in a drawing. Lines are used to represent edges, boundaries, and features of objects in engineering drawings.

**Characteristics of a Line:**

 
• **One-dimensional:** A line has length but no width or depth. This means it is purely a geometric construct without thickness.
 
• **Infinite or Finite:** A line can be infinite (in theoretical geometry) or finite (as represented in an engineering drawing).
 
• **Straight or Curved:** A line can be straight (linear) or curved, depending on the context and the requirements of the drawing.
 
• **Direction:** A line can be horizontal, vertical, or inclined, indicating the orientation of an object or feature.

**Importance in Engineering Drawings:**

 
• **Representation:** Lines are used to represent edges, contours, and boundaries of objects.
 
• **Communication:** They convey the dimensions, tolerances, and features of the design to engineers, manufacturers, and fabricators.
 
• **Types of Lines:** Different types of lines (e.g., solid, dashed, dotted) are used to represent various features such as visible edges, hidden edges, and centerlines.
 
• **Precision:** Lines in engineering drawings must be precise and accurate to ensure that the design can be manufactured correctly.

**Correct Option Analysis:**

The correct option is:

**Option 1:** A one-dimensional figure, which has length but no width.

This option correctly defines a line in the context of engineering drawings. A line is indeed a one-dimensional entity, characterized by having length but no width or depth. It is a fundamental geometric construct used to represent edges, contours, and other features in technical drawings
